Let \(t=\tau\), and write
\[
a=f_4(t)=(t,1/3,1/3)^T,\qquad b=f_5(t)=(1/3,t,1/3)^T.
\]

For any positive definite candidate \(M=\sum w_i f_i f_i^T\), the standard directional concavity criterion says it is optimal iff
\[
f_i^T M^{-1}f_i\le 3\qquad (i=1,\dots,5),
\]
with equality on every positive-weight support point. Indeed,
\[
\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\log\det\bigl((1-\varepsilon)M+\varepsilon f_if_i^T\bigr)\bigg|_{\varepsilon=0}
=f_i^TM^{-1}f_i-3.
\]

At
\[
w^0=\left(\frac13,\frac13,\frac13,0,0\right),
\qquad M_0=\frac13 I,
\]
we have
\[
f_1^TM_0^{-1}f_1=f_2^TM_0^{-1}f_2=f_3^TM_0^{-1}f_3=3,
\]
and
\[
a^TM_0^{-1}a=b^TM_0^{-1}b
=3\left(t^2+\frac29\right)=3t^2+\frac23.
\]
Thus \(w^0\) is optimal exactly when
\[
3t^2+\frac23\le 3
\iff t^2\le \frac79
\iff t\le \frac{\sqrt7}{3}.
\]
So
\[
\tau_c=\frac{\sqrt7}{3}.
\]

For uniqueness in this range: if another optimizer had the same optimal determinant, strict concavity in \(M\) forces the same matrix \(M_0=I/3\). But \(M_0\) has zero off-diagonal entries, while every off-diagonal contribution from \(f_4f_4^T\) or \(f_5f_5^T\) is positive when \(t>0\). Hence \(w_4=w_5=0\), and then necessarily \(w_1=w_2=w_3=1/3\). So the optimizer is uniquely
\[
\left(\frac13,\frac13,\frac13,0,0\right)
\]
for \(0<t\le \tau_c\).

Now take \(t=\tau_c+h\), \(h>0\) small. By the symmetry interchanging coordinates \(1,2\) and \(f_4,f_5\), the unique optimum is symmetric, so write
\[
w_1=w_2=x,\qquad w_3=z,\qquad w_4=w_5=y,
\]
with
\[
2x+z+2y=1.
\]
Set
\[
z=\frac13+v,\qquad x=\frac13-\frac v2-y.
\]
At \(h=0,y=0,v=0\), this is \(M_0\). Using
\[
\log\det(M_0+\Delta)
=\log\det M_0+\operatorname{tr}(3\Delta)
-\frac12\operatorname{tr}\bigl((3\Delta)^2\bigr)+O(\|\Delta\|^3),
\]
one obtains, uniformly for small \(h,y,v\),
\[
\Psi(t)+3\log3
=
4\sqrt7\,hy-\frac{27}{4}v^2-3vy
-\frac{94+8\sqrt7}{18}y^2
+o(h^2+y^2+v^2).
\]
For fixed \(y\), the quadratic part is maximized in \(v\) at
\[
v=-\frac29y.
\]
Substituting gives
\[
\Psi(t)+3\log3
=
4\sqrt7\,hy-\frac{44+4\sqrt7}{9}y^2+o(h^2+y^2).
\]
Hence the maximizing \(y\) satisfies
\[
y=\frac{9\sqrt7}{2(11+\sqrt7)}h+o(h),
\]
so in particular \(y>0\) for all sufficiently small \(h>0\). Therefore both \(w_4,w_5\) are positive just to the right of \(\tau_c\).

The maximal quadratic gain is
\[
\frac{(4\sqrt7)^2}{4\cdot \frac{44+4\sqrt7}{9}}h^2
=
\frac{63}{11+\sqrt7}h^2.
\]
Thus
\[
\lim_{h\downarrow0}
\frac{\Psi(\tau_c+h)-\Psi(\tau_c)}{h^2}
=
\frac{63}{11+\sqrt7}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{\sqrt7}{3},\frac{63}{11+\sqrt7}\right)}
\]
